extracted.intended_audience: entities seeking to register as the private-led traceback consortium; voice service providers; industry stakeholders and commenters in FCC TRACED Act rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and selection principles for establishing and registering a single private-led consortium to conduct traceback of suspected unlawful robocalls under section 13(d) of the TRACED Act, plus questions about identifying and mitigating providers that originate large-scale unlawful robocall campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Letter of Intent requirements (section 13(d)(1)(A)-(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: In its Letter of Intent, the entity must satisfy the statutory requirements by: (a) demonstrating that the consortium is a neutral third-party competent to manage the private-led effort to trace back the origin of suspected unlawful robocalls; (b) including a copy of the consortium’s written best practices, with an explanation thereof, regarding management of its traceback efforts and regarding providers of voice services' participation in the consortium's efforts; (c) certifying that, consistent with section 222(d)(2) of the Communications Act, the consortium’s efforts will focus on fraudulent, abusive, or unlawful traffic; and (d) certifying that the consortium has notified the Commission that it intends to conduct traceback efforts of suspected unlawful robocalls in advance of registration as the single consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Letter of Intent must include the entity's name and statement of intent to conduct private-led traceback efforts and to register with the Commission as the single consortium. Letters are filed in response to an annual public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality (consortium must be a neutral third party)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registered consortium must be a neutral third party and demonstrate openness indicating neutrality by explaining how it will allow voice service providers to participate in an unbiased, non-discriminatory, and technology-neutral manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openness is an indicator of neutrality; applicants should show internal structural, procedural, and administrative mechanisms that do not result in lack of neutrality. Neutrality does not require indiscriminate participation—consortiums may restrict or deny participation where there is a valid reason (e.g., to prevent entities that may evade traceback from gaining access). The Bureau will consider public input about alleged unfair discrimination. Examples of neutrality-related matters include executive committee composition, structural independence from advocacy entities, and avoidance of discriminatory participation fees. The Commission declines to mandate a single organizational structure for neutrality, preferring principles over prescriptive rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence to manage traceback efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: The registered consortium must be a competent manager of private-led efforts to trace back the origin of suspected unlawful robocalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competent management includes ability to effectively and efficiently manage traceback processes across multiple voice service providers, timely and successfully find origins of suspected unlawful robocalls that traverse multiple networks, work cooperatively across the industry, provide prompt and comprehensive information to the Bureau and other legitimate requestors, and conform to applicable legal requirements (e.g., confidentiality, subpoenas). Evidence of expertise and prior success in managing and improving traceback processes is relevant and may be weighed, but such experience is not a prerequisite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written best practices requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The registered consortium must maintain, and conform its actions to, written best practices regarding the management of private-led traceback efforts and regarding providers of voice services' participation in such efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written best practices should, at minimum, address compliance with statutory requirements and establish fair and reasonable processes/criteria for provider participation. They should explain how they demonstrate best practices. Relevant topics include (a) voice service provider participation rules, (b) how specific calls are selected for traceback, (c) traceback information sharing, (d) consortium governance, and (e) budget transparency (including participation fees). The Commission will not mandate specific best practices because best practices evolve, but will review and evaluate the offered practices and require prompt notice of material changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on fraudulent, abusive, or unlawful traffic (section 222(d)(2) consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consortium efforts must focus on 'fraudulent, abusive, or unlawful' traffic consistent with section 222(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation should consider scope, scale, and harm. Large-scale unlawful spoofing or robocalling that burdens networks or threatens infrastructure can be abusive. The definition of suspected unlawful robocalls includes calls the Commission or a provider reasonably believes violate section 227(b) or (e); not all such calls involve fraud. A consortium should adopt criteria consistent with these considerations to govern how calls are selected for traceback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and participation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Consortiums must explain how they will allow voice service providers to participate in an unbiased, non-discriminatory, and technology-neutral manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective criteria of openness are encouraged to promote broad participation. While openness is required, the consortium may objectively restrict participation (for example, to deny access to entities thought likely to evade traceback). The Bureau will evaluate participation procedures in determining neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation principle: use principles rather than prescriptive structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will set forth a set of principles for the Bureau to apply in selecting the registered consortium instead of prescribing a single detailed governance structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach balances statutory compliance with the need for a nimble, dynamic traceback process that can evolve with new schemes and technologies. The Bureau will select the entity that best meets statutory requirements and the Commission's principles; public input is welcome and specific examples are probative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection factors and weighting (expertise and success)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau may weigh a consortium's expertise and success in managing and improving traceback processes when selecting among applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expertise/success is relevant and reasonable to consider but is not a statutory prerequisite. Weighting such factors should not foreclose innovative entrants; the Commission encourages qualified entities to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural timeline and process for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Enforcement Bureau must issue, no later than April 28 of each year, an annual public notice seeking registration; the notice will set the deadline for submission of Letters of Intent; the Bureau will review Letters of Intent and select the single registered consortium no later than 90 days after the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the initial (2020) cycle, the Bureau will provide an opportunity for public comment on any Letter of Intent and set the filing date no sooner than 30 days after the rules are published in the Federal Register. The incumbent registrant need not resubmit a Letter of Intent after initial selection unless it wishes to change certifications; the incumbent's initial certifications continue in effect for subsequent years unless the incumbent notifies the Commission otherwise by the filing date set in the annual notice. In event of delays, incumbent may continue traceback efforts until effective date of new selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing compliance certifications and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity seeking registration must certify in the Letter of Intent that it will (1) remain in compliance throughout its tenure; (2) conduct an annual review to ensure compliance with statutory requirements; and (3) promptly notify the Commission of changes that reasonably bear on its certification, including material changes to best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau reserves the right to revisit requirements or impose additional commitments if necessary. The Commission encourages complaints and public input regarding the consortium's compliance and neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and transparency in selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau will allow public comment on Letters of Intent (at least in the initial cycle) and will consider public input when evaluating neutrality and other statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau has discretion to determine additional processes (e.g., public meetings where applicants can respond to questions) to ensure sufficient information to select the registered consortium. The Commission encourages entities that believe the consortium has unfairly discriminated to alert the Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call selection criteria for traceback
rubrics_metrics.description: Consortium written best practices should include criteria governing how specific calls are selected for traceback, considering scope, scale, and harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include prioritizing large-scale campaigns, calls that burden networks, or calls that pose significant consumer harm. The Commission expects consortia to explain selection criteria in their best practices; overly narrow definitions (e.g., only calls that perpetrate fraud) are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traceback information sharing and confidentiality/legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The consortium must provide prompt and appropriate information to the Bureau and other entities with a legitimate legal right to the information while conforming to legal requirements (e.g., confidentiality and subpoenas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium processes must recognize varying authorities of state Attorneys General and other entities; some recipients may require legal process to obtain information. Best practices should address how and to whom traceback information is shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget transparency and fee fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices should address consortium budgeting and transparency, including disclosure of participation fees or costs and demonstration that fees are not discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discriminatory fees could reflect lack of neutrality. Letters of Intent may include description of expected costs and funding sources; the Commission will consider transparency in evaluating neutrality and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria/questions for identifying providers that 'repeatedly originate large-scale unlawful robocall campaigns'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission seeks comment on standards the consortium should use to identify providers that repeatedly originate large-scale unlawful robocall campaigns, and how to define 'unlawful robocall,' 'campaign,' and 'large-scale.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include whether 'unlawful robocall' is narrower than 'suspected unlawful robocall' and what level of certainty is required, whether 'campaign' implies coordinated patterns, whether 'large-scale' should be based solely on call volume or also on factors like burden on networks or harm, and what thresholds/evidence should be required to designate a provider. The Commission solicits comment on these factors and objective criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential mitigation actions for identified providers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provider is identified as repeatedly originating large-scale unlawful campaigns, the Commission must require that provider to take actions to ensure it does not continue to originate such calls and must make reasonable efforts to minimize mitigation burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Further Notice asks whether to prescribe specific robocall mitigation practices, require close monitoring, require submission of compliance plans and periodic reports, require a point of contact (with e.g., 14-day response), implement know-your-customer obligations and report customer contact information to the consortium or Commission, require internal traffic-monitoring measures, and whether monitoring should be by the Commission, consortium, or independent third party. The Commission seeks comment on benefits, drawbacks, and burden-minimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incumbent registrant continuation and update process
rubrics_metrics.description: An incumbent registered consortium will not be required to refile a Letter of Intent after initial selection; the initial certifications continue for subsequent years unless the incumbent notifies the Commission otherwise by the filing date set in the annual notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a competing application is submitted, the incumbent will be notified and may be required to submit another application or an update describing any changes to operating procedures. Incumbent authorized to continue traceback efforts during selection delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on scope of consortium responsibilities (call blocking separate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of the consortium and its operation should not be used to decide broader call blocking policy or to address concerns best considered in separate FCC proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns about protecting legitimate calls and minimizing false positives are acknowledged but are more appropriately addressed in call blocking proceedings rather than in selecting the traceback consortium. The consortium itself will not engage in call blocking or labeling as part of its traceback role.
